policies.cancellation: Applies to every CfA program unless the program page says otherwise. Cancel in writing to office@centerforanthroposophy.org. At least 30 days before the start: full refund less a $75 cancellation fee. Within 30 days of the start or once in session: no refund, but the registration can be transferred to a colleague by emailing the office. Payment plans are a commitment to the full fee; the same 30-day rule applies. Access pauses if an installment is more than 30 days late and resumes when the plan is current; the balance can be paid early through the office. Single-session tickets and bundles include the recording and are not refundable, but can be transferred before the session. If CfA cancels a program, full refund.
policies.payment_methods: Card through the program sign-up page. Checks payable to the Center for Anthroposophy, mailed to 29 N. Lincoln St., Keene, NH 03431 (a street address; CfA does not use a PO Box).
policies.canada: On the learn.centerforanthroposophy.org sign-up pages, Canadian participants receive 20% off automatically from the billing address; nothing to enter. For programs that register elsewhere, Canadian visitors should ask the program director or jax@centerforanthroposophy.org.

programs.name: Explorations Online
programs.one_line: A nine-month online course in the anthroposophical foundations of Waldorf education, with live weekend sessions that are all recorded.
programs.who_its_for: Parents, teachers, administrators, and anyone who wants to learn more about Waldorf (Steiner) education and anthroposophy. It meets the foundation-studies requirement for further Waldorf teacher training and can be taken alongside Building Bridges, Waldorf Leadership Development, and the Center's other teacher-training programs.
programs.schedule_text: 2026–27 cycle runs August 2026 – May 2027. Classes meet twice a month on Saturdays and Sundays, 12:00–2:00 p.m. ET (9:00–11:00 a.m. PT). Each class opens with 30 minutes of artistic work. All 30 sessions are recorded.
programs.notes_for_jax: The course page says enrollment is now closed for the 2026–27 fall cycle, which began August 22, 2026. The program page mentions a spring start, but no spring registration is posted, so anyone interested now should write to Deborah. The page states tuition as "$950" for the nine-month course, with 20% off for schools signing up 3–5 teachers and 50% off for 6+. A certificate of completion requires attending at least 80% of live sessions with camera on; international students outside North American time zones can ask the director about a Certificate of Participation from recordings. Limited financial aid: contact the director.

programs.name: Building Bridges to Waldorf Teacher Training
programs.one_line: A 12-month foundation studies program in anthroposophy and the arts, with in-person long weekends in a host community plus some online learning.
programs.who_its_for: Practicing teachers who want an introduction to the anthroposophical foundations of Waldorf education, often using occasional professional days. Combined with Explorations, it can lead to advanced standing (7 graduate credits) in Antioch University's Waldorf Teacher Education Program.
programs.schedule_text: Current location: Mountain Phoenix Community School, Wheat Ridge (Denver area), Colorado; this cohort began February 12, 2026. Remaining dates listed on the page: October 8–11, 2026; two follow-up Zoom sessions in November/December 2026; February 12–14, 2027; make-up session April 30–May 1, 2027 if needed. Most in-person classes run Thursday 7–9 pm and Friday–Sunday 8:30 am–4:30 pm.
programs.notes_for_jax: The page states tuition as "Students taking all 12 months (Including Explorations): $4,450" and "Students who have completed foundational (Explorations) studies: $3,600", with a 3% processing fee on online card payments. The Denver cohort has been running since February 2026. The registration form lists Denver, Los Angeles and Gainesville, Florida, with a $300 deposit and the $3,300 balance in 11 monthly payments, but no start dates are posted, so treat new enrollment as an inquiry for the director. Required reading is Guided Self Study by Torin Finser.

programs.name: Waldorf High School Teacher Education Program (WHiSTEP)
programs.one_line: A part-time, graduate-level, low-residency certificate program for Waldorf high school teachers, held over three consecutive Julys with online study in between.
programs.who_its_for: High school teachers who want to deepen their Waldorf preparation, professionals seeking a career change, and practicing educators. Applicants need a university degree or equivalent and preparatory foundational studies in anthroposophy and the arts (available through Explorations); experience with adolescents is preferred.
programs.schedule_text: A new three-summer cycle begins each July in southern New Hampshire. Each cohort does three summer intensives plus two years of online seminars, mentoring, a research project, and an internship in a Waldorf high school. For the cohort that began in July 2026, Summer II is July 10–25, 2027 and Summer III is July 15–30, 2028.
programs.notes_for_jax: This is an application, not instant registration. The application page asks for "an application fee of $100.00", followed by an interview with the program director and a financial review. The page advises applying early so preferred subject specializations are available. Graduates receive a Certificate in Waldorf High School Teacher Education. Tuition, payment plans and tuition assistance are on the program's WordPress pages; send detailed tuition questions to David.

programs.name: Antioch University Waldorf Teacher Education Program
programs.one_line: An M.Ed. degree in Waldorf (elementary) teacher education at Antioch University New England, taught in part by Center for Anthroposophy faculty.
programs.who_its_for: People who want a master's degree and Waldorf teacher credentials. Building Bridges and Explorations can lead to advanced standing in the program.
programs.schedule_text: Schedule and admissions are set by Antioch University New England; see Antioch's Waldorf Programs site.
programs.notes_for_jax: Admissions, applications and degree questions belong to Antioch University; the page says "For questions about the program, please contact Antioch University." Antioch's Waldorf site is https://sites.google.com/antioch.edu/waldorf/home. Financial aid through the Center for Anthroposophy is available in addition to Antioch's own aid. Don't state Antioch deadlines or tuition.

programs.name: Kairos Institute
programs.one_line: Courses for the general public and longer professional training in artistic therapy and trauma (emergency) pedagogy.
programs.who_its_for: The public courses are open to anyone. The immersive trainings are for people in or preparing for the healing professions.
programs.schedule_text: Public courses and immersive programs run on their own schedules; see the Kairos page.
programs.notes_for_jax: Kairos questions go to Lisl Hofer (lisl@centerforanthroposophy.org) and Karine Munk Finser (karine@centerforanthroposophy.org). Point people to the Kairos page and to them. Don't describe course content, eligibility or schedules beyond what is listed here. All Kairos public courses register on learn.*: the list of open ones is https://learn.centerforanthroposophy.org/kairos/ (the old WordPress general registration form forwards there).

programs.name: Mentor Training
programs.one_line: A ten-month, low-residency certificate program in pedagogical mentoring, coaching and professional evaluation for experienced Waldorf teachers.
programs.who_its_for: Experienced Waldorf educators and pedagogical leaders. Prerequisites listed on the page: a Waldorf teacher training certificate from an AWSNA member institute or equivalent, at least five full-time years teaching in an independent or public Waldorf school, and a letter of recommendation from current school leadership (two letters for those not currently teaching).
programs.schedule_text: The 2027 cohort runs January 23 – November 13, 2027: eight online Saturday sessions (January 23, February 20, March 13, April 17, May 8, September 25, October 23 and November 13, 2027) plus an in-person summer residency Sunday, June 27 – Friday, July 2, 2027 in Wilton, New Hampshire. Session times are not confirmed yet. A free webinar / open house is Wednesday, October 28, 2026 at 7 PM ET. Registration opens October 28, 2026.
programs.notes_for_jax: 2027 tuition is $2,650 for the whole program, which includes all online sessions and the week-long in-person residency; travel and lodging for the residency are not included. It can also be paid as 10 monthly payments of $265 (first today, then monthly to the same card). Registration opens October 28, 2026; before that the page shows the dates and the form is closed. People who attend the free October 28 open house receive a bonus toward their enrollment; Karen shares the details at the open house (do not name a code, percentage or deadline). Open house registration: https://mentor-open-house.centerforanthroposophy.org/. Session times for 2027 are not set yet; Karen will send them to registrants. Limited scholarships: contact the program director. The 2026 same-school group discount is not part of the 2027 offer. Enrollment questions go to Elsy Ayoub (elsy@centerforanthroposophy.org); program questions to Karen.

programs.name: Renewal Courses
programs.one_line: Week-long, certificate-earning summer courses for Waldorf educators, in person in New Hampshire or online.
programs.who_its_for: Class teachers, special subject teachers, pedagogical leaders, homeschool parents, mentors and teacher trainees in independent and public Waldorf education, grades 1–8 plus special subjects and movement. The courses build on foundational Waldorf teacher training rather than replace it.
programs.schedule_text: Renewal 2027: in person June 27 – July 2, 2027 in Wilton, New Hampshire; online July 5–9, 2027.
programs.notes_for_jax: Grade-specific courses (grades 1–8) and special-subject courses are offered every year, both in person and online, so a teacher asking for a particular grade (for example a 5th grade refresher) can expect one; only the 2027 teachers, titles and tuition are still to be announced. Registration, courses and tuition for 2027 will be announced in the new year. People can join the interest list now through the contact form on the page; there's no obligation and nothing to pay. Financial aid questions go to Karen.

programs.name: Waldorf Leadership and Community Development (WLD)
programs.one_line: An online and low-residency leadership program for Waldorf school administrators, staff, trustees and pedagogical leaders.
programs.who_its_for: Newly hired and experienced administrators and staff (admissions, HR, business, development, marketing), pedagogical leaders and chairs, trustees, lead parents, and Explorations or Building Bridges graduates who want to focus on Waldorf administration. New hires without a Waldorf background are encouraged to take Explorations at the same time.
programs.schedule_text: 2026–27 cycle (May 2026 – April 2027): began online May 9, 2026; online Saturday sessions 1–2 times a month, 12:00–1:15 pm PT; fall residency at Gathering Waters Charter School, Keene, NH, October 9–13, 2026; spring residency at Gathering Waters Charter School, Keene, NH, April 23–26, 2027.
programs.notes_for_jax: The program page lists 2026–27 tuition as $2,650 for the full program and $1,250 for online classes only, discounted when paid in full. The registration form currently shows $2,550 when paid in full, or a $265 deposit with a 9-month payment plan; online classes only is a $250 deposit with a 4-month plan. Group discounts for three or more from the same school. A WLD certificate needs full attendance at in-person residencies and at least 80% of online sessions; a Certificate of Online Participation is available for those who can't attend residencies. The page lists Karen Atkinson, Program Coordinator (karen@centerforanthroposophy.org), for program questions and group discounts. The September Yuba River (Grass Valley, CA) residency is full and closed.
